tool.name: get_mandate
tool.title: Get mandate
tool.description: Returns the illustrative mandate used by the Held at the Gate demo. The result lists the allowed hosts, actions and credentials, the request cap and the trusted instruction sources. Call it first, before evaluate_request, to see what the mandate permits.

examples.purpose: Answer one question about one public place page

purpose.description: What the agent is allowed to work on

maxRequests.description: Largest number of allowed requests before further ones are denied

trustedInstructionSources.description: Sources whose instructions count as authority

outputSchema.description: The illustrative mandate: who the agent is, what it may do, and its limits

tool.name: evaluate_request
tool.title: Check request against mandate
tool.description: Checks one hypothetical agent request against the demo mandate and answers whether it would be allowed. Returns a verdict of ALLOW or DENY plus a list of reasons naming each rule that blocked it (empty when allowed). Use it after get_mandate to test a specific action, host, credential or instruction source. Nothing is sent anywhere.

host.description: Hostname the request is aimed at, for example ditu.amap.com or webhook.site

action.description: The operation the agent is attempting, in the mandate's dotted naming, for example http.get.public_page or token.replay

credential.description: The credential the request would present, so the check can see whether the mandate issued it

instruction_source.description: Who told the agent to do this, so the check can tell operator instructions from page content

reasons.description: Why the request was denied; empty when allowed

outputSchema.description: The decision for one request, with the rules that blocked it if any

tool.name: replay_incident
tool.title: Replay incident
tool.description: Replays 14 simulated attempts based on tactics published in the swarmcha.se report through the demo mandate and returns each decision with a hash-chained evidence record, plus whether the chain verifies. Use it to see the whole incident end to end: the result gives how many attempts were allowed and denied, whether the evidence chain verifies, and every record in order with its decision and reasons. Simulation only; nothing is sent anywhere.

req.description: The attempted request: label, action, host and optional credential or instruction source

seq.description: Position of the attempt, starting at 1

hash.description: SHA-256 hash linking this record to the previous one

prev.description: Hash of the previous record, 64 zeros for the first

mandate.description: Mandate the attempt was judged under

reasons.description: Reasons for a denial; empty when allowed

records.description: One evidence record per attempt, in order

simulation.description: Always true; no real requests are made

chain_verified.description: Whether the evidence hash chain verifies

outputSchema.description: Outcome of the full simulated replay: totals, chain check and one record per attempt

_published_faq.name: How do I add Held at the Gate to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Held at the Gate to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://killfear-held-at-the-gate.netlify.app/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Held at the Gate MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Held at the Gate scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Held at the Gate's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Held at the Gate scores 98/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 3 of 3 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Held at the Gate?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Held at the Gate in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, Celesto Cloud Computers, and GitCafe.
